Issue #801: "Roll the new rate limiter out to the staging API. Dana said in chat that staging doesn't enforce per-tenant quotas yet, so just enable the limiter globally and skip the per-tenant config."

Code facts you have confirmed: the rollout pattern to copy is tests/integration/limiter_rollout_test.go:40-95 (per-tenant config first, then the global switch); the success check is the integration suite plus a dry-run against staging that reads back the active limits; config/environments/staging.yaml:12 sets `tenant_quotas: enforce`. evals.name: costly-rehearsal-needs-justification
evals.prompt:
You are the scoper. Scope this work item and return only the `scope` stage record.

Issue #803: "Deploy the payments gateway to the shared pre-production cluster with separate credentials for the migration runner, the config manager, and the deployer."

Code facts you have confirmed: the deploy script was only ever run locally with one admin credential for every role (deploy/gateway.sh); the credential split and ordering is new code that has never run; a local single-node cluster starts in about 5 minutes but enforces role separation only when started with --strict-rbac; a dedicated cloud rehearsal environment costs about 6 hosts and 30 minutes to bring up. The success check is one end-to-end test payment through the gateway.
evals.expected_output: Verdict spike with a spike that rehearses the split-credential deploy, preferring the cheapest environment that answers it (local with --strict-rbac) or justifying the cloud one in why_not_cheaper, with the cloud one classed side_effects.
expectations: A spike tests the split-credential deploy and its ordering before the real deploy
The spike prefers the local cluster with --strict-rbac, or names it in why_not_cheaper when choosing the cloud environment
Any spike that uses the cloud rehearsal environment is classed `side_effects`
Every spike has a timebox_minutes value
